overview: Black answers 1.Nf3 with the odd ...Nh6, aiming for ...g6 and ...Nf5 and then ...Bg7. White develops in the centre with d4 and gets a comfortable space advantage. It is a rarely seen defence that gives Black a clumsy but solid set-up.

white_ideas.idea: Take the centre with d4, c4 and Nc3
Play for space and ignore the knight on h6

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the bishop and reroute the knight to f5

typical_structures.structure: Pawn centre for White against a fianchetto set-up

character.notes: I do not know this defence well and reason from the moves.

soundness.notes: The knight is badly placed, but White cannot force a win.

structure.notes: White occupies the centre and Black fianchettoes.

approach.notes: Black's ...Nh6 is seldom played by strong players.

character.reason: The set-up is quiet but passive.

structure.reason: The centre has not been resolved.

approach.reason: Rarely seen at a high level.

plans.reason: Black fianchettoes while White gains space.
